insights.summary: FY26 revenue rose 90% to ₹2,184 Cr and PAT 81% to ₹206 Cr, as AI systems grew 460% to 43% of revenue on large India AI Mission (strategic) orders. Management guided 35-40% revenue growth and a 13-14% operating EBITDA margin for the next couple of years, and starts FY27 with an order book of ₹2,100 Cr (₹2,400 Cr with L1 positions), more than last year's revenue. Inventory rose to 86 days to secure scarce components, and short-term borrowing rose to fund strategic orders.

what_changed.text: 35-40% revenue growth and 13-14% operating EBITDA margin for the next couple of years
New 15,000 sq ft facility for dense, liquid-cooled GPU systems
Promoters sold ~4% in February; no more sales for 12 months

We see a

analyst_questions.answer: Conflicting: CFO said enterprise-level; IR adviser said organic only, about 35%.
Adjusted for forex MTM, margins improved and are within guidance.
Not targeting them now; India is still a sovereign / neocloud market.
Short-term working capital for strategic orders.

red_flags.text: Inventory days up to 86 from 60; short-term borrowings up ~₹270 Cr.
Growth relies on lumpy government AI (strategic) orders.
Confusing answers on whether guidance includes strategic orders.

watch_next: Execution of the ₹1,600 Cr strategic order book

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Indian-designed high-end computing systems: AI GPU servers and clusters, HPC supercomputers, private cloud / HCI, plus software stacks (Tyrone brand)
business_snapshot.customers: Government (India AI Mission, NSM), research institutions, cloud providers like Yotta, large enterprises; ~50% government, 50% enterprise
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: FY26: AI systems 43%, HPC ~24%, private cloud ~24%, others; exports ~5%
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Sovereign AI compute, India AI Mission GPU tenders, data-centre build-out, NSM 2.0
